full_text:
Every year around this time, I release a rookie series that rivals *The Catcher in the Rye* in word count. This year I still spent countless hours researching the class… but I finally listened to my readers and kept it concise.

Here’s the culmination of my entire offseason of rookie research — in under 2,500 words.

Scott Barrett’s 2026 Post-Draft Superflex TE Premium Rookie Rankings
--------------------------------------------------------------------

#### Tier 1

__1\. Jeremiyah Love, Cardinals (RB1)__ — A hair behind Bijan Robinson as a prospect. In 1QB dynasty, I honestly might rather have Love than any three other players in this class combined.

{{PAYWALL}}

#### Tier 2

__2\. Fernando Mendoza, Raiders (QB1)__ — Old-school throwback QB who feels like he was built in a lab to be Tom Brady’s protégé, Kirk Cousins’ understudy, and the ultimate McShanahan-system QB.

__3\. Carnell Tate, Titans (WR1)__ — Analytically, it’s hard to say how good Tate is, other than to say that he’s not as good as Jeremiah Smith, which is also true of every WR in this year’s class. He doesn’t have the most fantasy-friendly archetype in this class, but Brett Whitefield and the NFL both seem to think he’s the best WR in this year’s class.

__4\. Jordyn Tyson, Saints (WR2)__ — Tyson was my model’s favorite WR from this class, and even Brett (who has him ranked as his WR4) would agree that Tyson has the most upside. He carries more risk than Tate, but more upside as well.

__5\. KC Concepcion, Browns (WR3)__ — [Brett’s WR2](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/prospect-guide/profiles/rookie/wr#/) based on film. Profiles somewhere between Brandon Aiyuk and a rich man’s Zay Flowers. Expect [Zay Flowers usage](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2047503236370677990?s=20) in this Todd Monken offense, which should help mitigate QB-play concerns in PPR leagues.

__6\. Jadarian Price, Seahawks__ __(RB2)__ — Any reservations regarding Price’s prospect profile get wiped out by the Round 1 draft capital, plus basically no backfield competition until Charbonnet returns (mid-November). But if you’re not RB-needy, try to sell this pick.

#### Tier 3

\> For fantasy, I think this is one of the worst rookie drafts in recent memory. Worst in at least 12-plus years and by a pretty good margin, I think. As I said pre-Draft, it [reminds me a lot of 2016 if you took out Derrick Henry from that year’s class](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2048096784581578828?s=20). I’m not sure if this is where things start to get really gross for me — that might be in the next tier — but, at the very least, this is where I’m a lot lower on the class than everyone else. If I can trade away the 1.07 for Parker Washington, Rome Odunze, or Michael Pittman, I’m probably going to be doing that. But I’d bet you can get away with a 1.07 for Washington/Odunze/Pittman-plus right now.

__7\. Makai Lemon, Eagles (WR4)__ — We were already low on the slot-only Lemon. This landing spot makes it worse. Run-heavy offense, a lot of 12 personnel, and a QB who doesn’t throw over the middle. \[[1](https://x.com/DynastyZoltanFF/status/2047496965936591013?s=20), [2](https://x.com/ffdataroma/status/2047673161395716566?s=20)\] I’d bet one of your leaguemates likes him more than I do.

__8\. Kenyon Sadiq, Jets (TE1)__ — Sadiq’s [production profile](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2033937403891830859?s=20) left much to be desired, but he’s still an all-time freak athlete with Round 1 draft capital. I think he’ll be a good player for a long time — I’m just not convinced he has true difference-making fantasy upside.

#### Tier 4

__9\. Eli Stowers, Eagles (TE2)__ — Stowers is Sadiq with a much wider range of outcomes. Most likely, he lands somewhere on the Mike Gesicki / Dalton Kincaid spectrum, but there’s also a real chance he’s Trey McBride lite once the Eagles move on from Goedert.

__10\. Ty Simpson, Rams (QB2)__ — Sean McVay QB” sounds great. But this is a guy who basically didn’t play in college, and now the Rams [might redshirt his entire rookie contract](https://x.com/adamwells1985/status/2047733890186432870?s=20). Maybe he’s the next Jordan Love. He’s probably just dead roster weight for you the next few years.

__11\. Omar Cooper Jr., Jets (WR5)__ — I was “meh” on Cooper the prospect, and I really don’t love this landing spot (slot WR in a 12-personnel-heavy offense), but Round 1 draft capital is no joke, even [in this economy](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2014869156382863719?s=20).

#### Tier 5

\> Do any of these players offer more long-term fantasy upside than what you got from a Tank Bigsby, Alexander Mattison, Marvin Jones Jr., or Mohamed Sanu? I’m not sure. And that makes me really sad.

__12\. Denzel Boston, Browns (WR6)__ — Betting on talent (Brett’s WR3) and hoping Cleveland figures out QB by 2027.

__13\. Germie Bernard, Steelers (WR7)__ — Bernard profiled as the sort of poor man’s Makai Lemon, but there wasn’t a very big difference in draft capital between them, and [the landing spot](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2048140386502406353?s=20) was arguably better for Bernard.

__14\. Jonah Coleman, Broncos (RB3)__ — The NFL was lower on him than I was, but I still think he offers among the most upside in this class.

__15\. Antonio Williams, Commanders (WR8)__ — Underrated analytically — he led Clemson in receiving as an 18-year-old true freshman and then had 75-904-11 in 2024 before disappointing in 2025 (due to a bad hamstring injury) — and then went to an ideal landing spot (competing with Treylon Burks and Luke McCaffrey for WR2 duties) with better-than-expected draft capital.

#### Tier 6

\> ”[The Disgusting Brothers](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4WqszvtVTF8)” tier.

__16\. De'Zhaun Stribling, 49ers (WR9)__ — My model hated this pick, but this is still nearly (one pick away from being) Round 1 draft capital for a player in a Kyle Shanahan offense.

__17\. Chris Bell, Dolphins (WR10)__ — A [potential top-20 pick](https://x.com/Schultz_Report/status/2034336561945596132?s=20) before suffering an ACL injury in November. Brett saw Round 1 talent based on his film. Even if he won’t be ready by Week 1, there’s plenty of upside for him in this offense, given Miami’s league-worst WR room.

__18\. Kaelon Black, 49ers (RB4)__ — One of the biggest IRL reaches I can remember (Black wasn’t even invited to the Combine), but he was still drafted as the RB3 in this year’s class, and we know “the Christian McCaffrey handcuff” is a valuable role.

__19\. Zachariah Branch, Falcons (WR11)__ — I started off as a hater, but this Draft from Hell has pushed me into the upside camp. Yeah, 51 of his 81 catches were screens — but “screen fraud” is still better than “complete fraud.”

#### Tier 7

\> The “I’m in excruciating physical pain typing this all out” tier.

__20\. Eli Raridon, Patriots (TE3)__ — Max Toscano’s TE1 because he’s a freak athlete, a very high-end blocker, and a [much better pass catcher than he gets credit for](https://x.com/maxtoscano1/status/2033759016803807473?s=20).

__21\. Elijah Sarratt, Ravens (WR12)__ — Analytics darling who my model thought was much better than almost a dozen WRs drafted ahead of him. He could feast for fantasy in a big slot role, which GM Eric DeCosta [hinted at](https://x.com/MattHarmon_BYB/status/2048517193910853698?s=20) in his post-Draft presser.

__22\. Oscar Delp, Saints (TE4)__ — Brett says there’s a 15-20% chance he’s “the next George Kittle.” Even if I don’t really agree, that’s more upside and better odds than most players in this class.

__23\. Carson Beck, Cardinals (QB3)__ — I’m sure he stinks, but there’s also a really good chance he’s Arizona’s starting QB in December.

__24\. Ted Hurst, Buccaneers (WR13)__ — Potential diamond in the rough, coming from Georgia State. [All-time freak athlete](https://x.com/gregauman/status/2047883570627084709?s=20), good draft capital, and a great landing spot. Steve Smith’s favorite WR in the class; [comp’d to Larry Fitzgerald](https://x.com/SteveSmithSr89/status/2047875865669693816?s=20).

__25\. Mike Washington Jr., Raiders (RB5)__ — I hated his analytics profile, but Brett liked the film. He’s also an all-time freak athlete (97.0 SPORQ), and probably already Las Vegas’ RB2.

__26\. Emmett Johnson, Chiefs (RB6)__ — He’s a subpar athlete (23.4 SPORQ) and just a one-year wonder, but he had 251 carries, 46 receptions, 1,821 YFS, and 15 total touchdowns last year at Nebraska, and Kenneth Walker is one of the most injury-prone RBs in football.

__27\. Nicholas Singleton, Titans (RB7)__ — It feels gross ranking a Round 5 RB this high, but [Ryan Heath loves Singleton’s upside](https://www.fantasypoints.com/nfl/articles/2026/ryan-heaths-rookie-rb-rankings), and this was a fairly ideal landing spot.

__28\. Kaytron Allen, Commanders (RB8)__ — Just a Round 6 pick, but this was a best-possible landing spot; the Commanders want to lean extremely run-heavy this year (that’s why Dan Quinn fired Kliff Kingsbury), and Rachaad White (RB1), Jacorey Croskey-Merritt (RB2), and Jerome Ford (RB3) won’t strike fear into anyone’s heart.

__28\. Malachi Fields, Giants (WR14)__ — [Historically unproductive](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2036171292076826978?s=20) with an awful [J.J. Arcega-Whiteside-like archetype](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2039016117738582105?s=20) in terms of how he wins, but the Giants were much higher on him than I was, giving up serious draft capital to land him in Round 3.

#### Tier 8

\> The “Do I Even Have Players Worth Dropping?” tier.

__30\. Kevin Coleman, Dolphins (WR15)__ — Coleman went outside of the top-175 picks, but he was one of my favorite sleeper WRs in this year’s class. This will sound crazy until you check out the depth chart — but he really might be Miami’s best WR.

__31\. Brenen Thompson, Chargers (WR16)__ — Thompson would rank 15 spots lower if his OC didn’t compare him to DeSean Jackson and Tyreek Hill, but alas… that’s [a real thing that actually happened](https://x.com/CoachspeakIndex/status/2048512919697297820?s=20).

__32\. Skyler Bell, Bills (WR17)__ — Feasted at UConn at age >21 up against a pillow-soft schedule, but hey, at least he actually feasted. Beyond that, landing spots don’t get much better than Buffalo.

__33\. Ja’Kobi Lane, Ravens (WR18)__ — Had 3X as many TDs as Makai Lemon and Zachariah Branch combined in 2024, but fell off in 2025. The draft capital was good, but Ravens GM Eric DeCosta seemed more excited to talk about Elijah Sarratt, whom he took a round later.

__34\. Max Klare, Rams (TE5)__ — I always want to be placing a premium on players tied to a Sean McVay offense, even if Klare is joining the most stacked TE room in the country.

__35\. Tanner Koziol, Jaguars (TE6)__ — Koziol is sort of like this year’s Oronde Gadsden. He led the FBS in receptions over the last two years, with more YPG than Carnell Tate. The Round 5 draft capital suggests he’s not any good, and he probably isn’t. But if he is, he’ll be amazing for fantasy. Those are often my favorite bets to make.

__36\. Adam Randall, Ravens (RB9)__ — WR convert who immediately led Clemson’s backfield. Workhorse size, legit athleticism, and [a Steve Bisciotti teacher’s pet](https://x.com/MySportsUpdate/status/2048488199148683387?s=20).

__37\. Taylen Green, Ravens (QB4)__ — Ran a 4.36 at the Combine and has 1,800+ rushing yards over the past two seasons. If he ever starts an NFL game, the fantasy upside is massive. But the over/under is probably 0.5 career NFL starts based on the Round 6 draft capital. Then again, he’s competing with Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson for playing time.

__38\. Eli Heidenreich, Steelers (RB10)__ — Just trust me, bro.

__39\. Chris Brazzell, Panthers (WR19)__ — Even if Carolina drafted him to be their [sacrificial X](https://x.com/ChrisWechtFF/status/2048152841122910383?s=20), his freakish athleticism plus Round 3 draft capital should hint at real upside long-term.

__40\. Bryce Lance, Saints (WR20)__ — [Christian Watson clone](https://x.com/RyanJ_Heath/status/2028595879829991763?s=20) athletically. Don’t expect anything in the short term, but the athleticism hints at upside in the long term.

__41\. Justin Joly, Broncos (TE7)__ — Pops in a bunch of efficiency metrics and outproduced K.C. Concepcion in 2024. Maybe he lucks into an Evan Engram-type role when Engram walks in 2027.

__42\. Caleb Douglas, Dolphins (WR21)__ — Even if he was a colossal reach irl, he was still a top-75 overall pick, selected by the most WR-needy team in the league.

__43\. Marlin Klein, Texans (TE8)__ — Even if he’s probably a much better blocker than pass-catcher (although maybe it’s hard to tell because Michigan’s passing game is so bad), Klein was still a top-60 overall pick.

__44\. Drew Allar, Steelers (QB5)__ — He’s not good at football, but he’s still a Round 3 pick competing for a starting job up against Mason Rudolph and Will Howard, not including a 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers.

__45\. Sam Roush, Bears (TE9)__ — It’s hard to imagine a pathway to fantasy relevancy behind Colston Loveland and Cole Kmet, but this is still one of Brett Whitefield’s favorite players in this year’s class. Maybe he can luck into an Isaiah Likely-like runout.

__46\. Terion Stewart, Chiefs (RB11)__ — 24-year-old UDFA but also one of the [most efficient runners in PFF College history](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2037597268610584758?s=20). Kansas City’s RB1 is the most injury-prone RB in football. Their RB2 is either Brashard Smith, Emmett Johnson, or Shunderrick Powell.

__47\. Cade Klubnik, Jets (QB6)__ — Worse than Beck and Allar, but no one would be shocked if he’s starting all of December once the Jets are already out of playoff contention.

__48\. Jack Endries (TE10)__ — Brett and I both saw Endres as a slightly poorer man’s Roush. Apparently, the NFL thought destitute man’s Rosuh, but the landing spot is nice.

__49\. Jeff Caldwell, Chiefs (WR22)__ — UDFA but also the [freakiest WR athlete since Calvin Johnson](https://x.com/ScottBarrettDFB/status/2046388446244249685?s=20). I’ll keep chasing longshot Chiefs WRs just because of the upside and the lack of real competition in that room.

__50\. Jaren Kanak, Titans (WR23)__ — The NFL probably thinks he’s a positionless tweener who can only contribute on special teams. But I saw quite a bit more upside for this freak athlete.
